audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Fizz all seven rows while content and the packet both gave Azir levels 6, first item and 2+ items — and the full layer's own whys for those three rows described Azir winning them.
audit.why: The row said Fizz and the sentence under it said 'Emperor's Divide online — the dive insurance', 'Nashor's spike', 'Full build Azir is a teamfight'. Three rows argued with themselves.
audit.corrected: Rows 4-6 moved to Azir, matching content and the packet, with each why rewritten to state why in Fizz terms (550 Urchin Strike, 400 hop, 120s fish).

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] put Chum the Waters at level 3 ('near 6'), and spikes[2].text credited the first-item spike to 'Conquer the Sands'.
audit.why: His ult does not exist at level 3, and Azir's Q is Conquering Sands — 'Conquer the Sands' is a fabricated name and it appeared in the mid prose too.
audit.corrected: Level 3 explained by Seastone Trident's reset and Nimble Fighter; the item spike named Nashor's Tooth against his 550 dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nimble Fighter appeared nowhere on the page, and breakdown.cooldowns carried no number.
audit.why: Riot's text: Fizz moves through units and takes a flat amount of reduced damage from all sources. Azir's damage arrives as many small soldier hits, so a flat per-instance reduction is worth more against Azir than against almost anyone — and 'moves through units' is why a soldier line never body-blocks him. Playful / Trickster is untargetable on a 16s cooldown at rank 1, Urchin Strike is 550 range on 8s, Chum the Waters is 1300 range on 120s.
audit.corrected: Nimble Fighter's flat reduction written into the trade rules, the carry line and the level 3-5 spike; real cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns and the do's.
sources: brief enemyKit passive/Q/E/R text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: The derived flags on this brief mark Playful / Trickster and Chum the Waters as 'grounding'.
audit.why: Riot's own text for both abilities says nothing about grounding — the hop is untargetable and the fish slows and knocks up. Grounding would matter enormously here (it would disable Shifting Sands), so a wrong flag is worse than no flag.
audit.corrected: Nothing asserted about grounding anywhere in the edits; the untargetable window and the knockup are stated instead, both of which are in the text.

notes: Nimble Fighter was missing from the entire page and it is the reason Azir's chip underperforms here: Fizz takes a flat cut from every damage instance, and Azir's damage arrives as many small soldier hits, so trickled autos are the worst value in the matchup. It also explains why a soldier line never body-blocks him — he moves through units. 'Conquer the Sands' was a fabricated name for Azir's Conquering Sands and appeared twice (spikes[2].text and mid); both fixed. Chart: the full layer said Fizz for all seven rows while its own whys for rows 4-6 described Azir winning them, and both content and the packet give Azir those rows — flipped the sides and rewrote the whys. WARNING for the flag pipeline: this brief marks Playful / Trickster AND Chum the Waters as 'grounding', which Riot's text does not support for either. I asserted nothing about grounding; if that flag is trusted elsewhere it would wrongly tell an Azir his E is disabled. phases[N].rating left untouched — see questions.
